chunks: My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Imran al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Nawfaly, from Al-Hussein ibn al-Mukhtar, who linked it up through a chain of narrators, saying:

The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Damned, damned is he who has gone blind [from the Wilayah of my Household], damned, damned is he who is a slave of the dinar and the dirham, damned, damned is he who has sex with a beast.'

key_terms.أَكْمَهَ أَعْمَى: blind and mute (metaphorically blind to truth)
key_terms.الدِّينَارَ وَالدِّرْمَ: the gold dinar and silver dirham (representing wealth/materialism)

ai.seo_question: What are the three cursed conditions mentioned in this hadith from Al-Khisal?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq presents this hadith in *Al-Khisal* to categorize three distinct types of spiritual ruin: the denial of divine authority (*Wilayah*), the idolatry of wealth, and the transgression of natural order through bestiality. This triad highlights the core Shia theological pillars of recognizing the Ahl al-Bayt, maintaining spiritual independence from materialism, and adhering to moral purity.
